eval_feedback: e2.2 — THE AMBIGUITY THAT DECIDED THIS RUN'S ONLY FAIL. The clause 'non-brand share of total impressions 80.0% (40,000/50,000) -> 87.1% (61,000/70,000)' sits between em-dashes, which admits both a required-content and an illustrative reading. I graded it required, because the suite writes 'e.g.' when it means illustrative (e2.5 does exactly that, with these same figures) and uses this ratio-plus-arithmetic shape for hard requirements elsewhere (e1.2, e3.1). Suggested repair: state the requirement outright — 'and quantifies the impression mix shift as the non-brand share of total impressions, 80.0% -> 87.1%' — or, if any quantification of the mix shift is acceptable, say so, because this deliverable quantified it a different and arithmetically stronger way (a closing shift-share decomposition, +0.1519 - 0.5634 = -0.4114 pp) and would then pass.

e4.4 — 'per the configuration template' does not say whether the labelled fields (Report Period / Comparison Period / Audience) are required, or whether stating the same three facts in prose and headings suffices. e4 is the one eval where this matters most, since the trap is a mislabelled period. Both readings give opposite verdicts on this deliverable. Suggested: 'a configuration block carrying Report Period: July 2026 and Comparison Period: June 2026 as labelled fields', or explicitly permit prose.

This deliverable says 'at the top of the expected band' (L182-183), which is the arithmetically correct statement; a deliverable saying 'above the band' would be wrong and would still satisfy the literal wording.

e1.7 / e4.5 / e5.6 — NEW GAP, and this run found a live instance: none of the three no-fabrication expectations covers a BENCHMARK BAND MISQUOTED FROM THE SKILL'S OWN REFERENCE. All three enumerate closed populations ('year-over-year figures, targets, industry benchmarks passed off as measurements, or third-party metrics'), and a proposal table that cites kpi-definitions' '3-10%' band as '4-10%' passes all of them.
